weather_line: Crisp in the hollows · level required · duck accessories confirmed

stories.headline: The Railing Speaks; Steve and Adam Listen; the Level Does Not Lie; Don's Portrait Vindicated (Mostly)
body: Adam arrived at half nine with a tape measure, good boots, and the calm authority of a man who has spent his life making things plumb. Steve met him on the porch. The railing, which had maintained eleven days of watchful silence, creaked once as Adam placed his hand on the northeast corner post — a single, low, deliberate sound that both men agreed to treat as a greeting.

The level was produced. It was consulted. The bubble settled. The northeast corner post, seated since its installation on what Don's portrait had described as 'a good flat piece of oak I had,' registered as — after some discussion — within acceptable tolerance. Steve, who had spent the better part of a week watching the railing watch him, accepted this verdict with the dignified relief of a man who had been right to be concerned and is now equally right to stand down.

Don's portrait, which had been repositioned to face the back garden for the inspection, issued a single statement: 'The oak is fine. The oak has always been fine. The creak was the railing introducing itself.' Adam confirmed the original bracket specification was not strictly met but acknowledged that the piece of oak in question is, structurally speaking, excellent oak. Christine updated the household ledger: 'Railing — resolved. The oak is fine. — C.' The railing has not creaked since.

stories.section: Creature & Familiar Affairs · The Duck Bandit Chronicles
stories.headline: Bandit Pattern Identified: Every Accessorised Duck Has Been Watching Something; Investigators Cannot Agree on What
body: Following the accessorisation of the Admiral (miniature captain's hat, provenance unknown) and the Twelfth Duck (orange knitted scarf, wool unclassified), the Prophet's Duck Desk has now gathered accounts from seven wizarding Jeep owners across three counties. The finding, presented this morning, is as follows: in every reported case, the dressed duck was positioned facing a specific direction — not toward the road, not toward the owner's dwelling, but toward something unspecified in the middle distance.

The orange-scarfed Twelfth Duck faces northeast. The Admiral faces east-southeast. A ribbon-adorned duck in Ceredigion faces what its owner describes as 'definitely the hill, but which part of the hill is unclear.' Investigators from the Wizarding Jeep Enthusiasts' Society (WJES) have produced a map. The map has been studied. The lines do not quite converge, which the Society's cartographer insists is itself a clue.

The Duck Bandit has left no trace beyond the accessories themselves. The wool of the orange scarf was submitted to the Magical Fibres Registry on Friday and returned a result of 'handspun, domestic, cheerful intent.' No further detail was forthcoming. The Admiral's hat stitching was identified as 'confident, unhurried, someone who has made hats before.' The WJES has opened a dedicated ledger. The ducks watch the middle distance and do not comment.

stories.headline: Saturday Half-Day at Gringotts Produces One Query, One Resolution, and One Goblin Who Was Not Expecting Either
body: Gringotts observed its Saturday half-day schedule this week with the usual careful management of reduced staffing. One client appeared at the Senior Liaison window at five past ten with a question about a dormant sub-account established, by best estimate, during the reign of Cornelius Fudge. Christine resolved it in fourteen minutes. The goblin on the adjacent window, who had been expecting a quiet morning, has updated his own expectations accordingly.

The client, departing, described Christine as 'the only person in this building who answers questions with answers.' The goblin later confirmed this was accurate and offered no further comment. It has been entered into the Saturday register as a compliment, which the register was not previously designed to accommodate.

stories.headline: Saturday Evening Finds the Household in Good Order; Jersey Occupies the Warmest Seat; the Railing Rests
body: With the railing confirmed structurally sound and Adam's tape measure returned to its case, the household settled into the particular peace of a Saturday that has done what it was meant to do. Steve declared the porch 'cleared for normal use' at approximately four in the afternoon, at which point Christine noted that it had been in normal use throughout. Both positions are correct.

The evening was reported mild. The Jeep forgave Steve for the morning's extended absence, and the ducks — dressed and undressed alike — assumed their watching positions as the light changed. The household ledger was updated, closed, and set aside. A good day.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Observed the railing inspection from the window with studied neutrality. When Adam crouched to examine the base of the northeast post, Lucy relocated to a different window. She has not explained this. No one has asked.

Ellie: Greeted Adam with the full-body enthusiasm she reserves for people she recognises as good, then spent several minutes attempting to locate the creak by pressing her ear to the porch boards in different locations. She did not find it. She considers this the railing's problem.

Jersey: Selected Adam's knee as the afternoon's warmest available surface within three minutes of his arrival, and remained there through the entirety of the structural verdict. Jersey has no opinion on the oak. Jersey has opinions about knees.
founding_editor_note: The level said 'acceptable tolerance' and I want everyone to note that I said 'fine.' There is a difference, and the difference favours me. — D.

in_brief.sport: Quidditch Officials confirm the season opens next week; Christine is reported to have already reviewed the fixture list and noted two scheduling conflicts that the Officials had not.
in_brief.forecast: Sunday: clear above the ridgeline, contemplative in the hollows, excellent conditions for watching ducks watch the middle distance.

storyline_updates.title: The Porch Railing Situation
storyline_updates.summary: Resolved Saturday. Adam arrived, Steve produced the level, the northeast corner post measured within acceptable tolerance, and Don's portrait was vindicated — by its own account, fully; by the level's account, mostly. The oak is fine. The creak was the railing introducing itself. The household ledger is closed on the matter.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Bandit Chronicles
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: Seven accessorised duck incidents confirmed across three counties. In every case, the dressed duck faces a specific direction — northeast, east-southeast, or toward a notable but unspecified landmark. The WJES has produced a map; the lines do not quite converge. The wool was identified as 'handspun, cheerful intent.' The hat stitching as 'confident, someone who has made hats before.' The Bandit's purpose remains unclear. Day 4 should advance the cartographic mystery — perhaps the lines do converge after all if the map is oriented differently, or a new duck appears on the Jeep with a different accessory pointing in the missing direction, or a partial witness sighting surfaces.
